votes.measure: S.Amdt. 87 (as modified) to S.Amdt. 2 to S.1
votes.title: Hoeven sense-of-Congress amendment on climate change (Keystone XL Pipeline Act)
votes.what_it_did: Would have stated the sense of Congress that climate change is real and that human activity contributes to climate change.

votes.title: Schatz sense-of-Congress amendment on climate change (Keystone XL Pipeline Act)
votes.what_it_did: Would have stated the sense of Congress that climate change is real and that human activity significantly contributes to climate change.

votes.title: Senate passage of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022
votes.what_it_did: Budget reconciliation bill that included clean-energy and climate tax credits and spending, along with health-care and tax provisions.

votes.title: Senate passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act
votes.what_it_did: Budget reconciliation bill that, among many tax and spending provisions, repealed or accelerated the termination of several IRA clean-energy tax credits (e.g., wind and solar facilities must begin construction before July 5, 2026 or begin producing electricity before January 1, 2028 to qualify for the clean electricity credits; EV credits ended for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025), per CRS Insights IN12624 and IN12625.

votes.title: CRA disapproval of EPA Waste Emissions Charge (methane fee) rule
votes.what_it_did: Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving EPA's rule implementing the Waste Emissions Charge for petroleum and natural gas systems.

votes.title: CRA disapproval of EPA waiver for California Advanced Clean Cars II
votes.what_it_did: Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving EPA's Clean Air Act preemption waiver for California's Advanced Clean Cars II vehicle emission standards.

votes.title: Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 - motion to concur in the Senate amendment
votes.what_it_did: Final House approval of the budget reconciliation bill enacted as the Inflation Reduction Act, which created and expanded clean-energy and climate tax credits and programs.

votes.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act - motion to concur in the Senate amendment
votes.what_it_did: Final House passage of the FY2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21), which among many provisions repealed the IRA electric-vehicle credits for vehicles acquired after Sept. 30, 2025, repealed the residential clean energy credit after 2025, and required wind and solar facilities to begin construction before July 5, 2026 or be placed in service before 2028 to claim the clean electricity credits (CRS Insights IN12624 and IN12625, https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/IN/PDF/IN12624/IN12624.2.pdf ; https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/IN/PDF/IN12625/IN12625.2.pdf).

votes.title: Congressional Review Act disapproval of EPA Waste Emissions Charge rule for petroleum and natural gas systems - passage
votes.what_it_did: House passage of a CRA resolution disapproving EPA's rule implementing the methane Waste Emissions Charge on oil and gas facilities.

votes.title: Congressional Review Act disapproval of EPA waiver for California Advanced Clean Cars II - passage
votes.what_it_did: House passage of a CRA resolution disapproving EPA's Clean Air Act preemption waiver for California's Advanced Clean Cars II vehicle emission standards.

notes: Member-by-member votes are transcribed from the official senate.gov roll-call pages listed in each vote's source_url; per-vote tallies were re-counted and match the official totals (and 2015 votes were spot-checked against the senate.gov XML).
Roster = the 100 senators listed on senate.gov/senators as of 2026-11-25 (page metadata dated 2026-11-10): 53 R, 45 D, 2 I.

Alan Armstrong (R-OK) was appointed March 24, 2026 to the seat vacated by Markwayne Mullin (confirmed as Homeland Security Secretary); he serves through the end of the term. He is 'Not in office' for all six votes (Mullin voted Yea on OBBBA, H.J.Res. 35 and H.J.Res. 88). Source: PBS NewsHour, https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/energy-executive-alan-armstrong-picked-to-fill-mullins-senate-seat-through-end-of-year

Darline Graham (R-SC) was appointed in July 2026 after Sen. Lindsey Graham died in office; she is 'Not in office' for all six votes. Lindsey Graham's votes (not recorded here) were Yea, Yea, Nay, Yea, Yea, Yea. Source: NPR, https://www.npr.org/2026/07/13/nx-s1-5891839/lindsey-graham-senate-seat-darline-graham

Jon Husted (R-OH) lost the Nov. 3, 2026 special election to Sherrod Brown but remains in office; per a Nov. 13, 2026 report, Ohio certifies by Dec. 4 and Husted's appointed term runs to Dec. 15 under state law. Source: https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/ohios-us-senator-elect-sherrod-brown-could-get-early-start-washington

S.Amdt. 87 and S.Amdt. 58 were considered under a 60-vote threshold (3/5 'required for majority' on the roll-call pages); both were rejected despite majority support. Roll-call numbers: Hoeven 87 = vote 11 (4:42 PM), Schatz 58 = vote 12 (5:03 PM).

Nuance on the 2015 amendments: some senators voted Nay on one for reasons other than rejecting climate science, e.g. Bernie Sanders voted Nay on Hoeven 87 (which said human activity 'contributes') but Yea on Schatz 58 ('significantly contributes'). The 'anti_position' coding treats any Nay as the anti position.

Amendment text: Hoeven 87 as modified, Congressional Record Jan. 21, 2015 (S311 ff.), https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CREC-2015-01-21/html/CREC-2015-01-21-pt1-PgS311.htm; Schatz 58 'significantly contributes' wording as quoted by AIP FYI, https://www.aip.org/fyi/2015/record-key-senate-vote-climate-change (the senate.gov page gives only the purpose 'To express the sense of Congress regarding climate change').
IRA (H.R. 5376) and OBBBA (H.R. 1) Senate passage votes were each 50-50 with the Vice President voting Yea to break the tie.

OBBBA clean-energy note sources: CRS Insight IN12624, 'IRA Tax Credit Repeal in the FY2025 Reconciliation Law: Part 1' (Dec. 12, 2025), https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/IN/PDF/IN12624/IN12624.2.pdf ; CRS Insight IN12625 (Part 2), https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/IN/PDF/IN12625/IN12625.2.pdf . These describe the enacted law, P.L. 119-21 (July 4, 2025).

H.J.Res. 88 also had a motion-to-proceed vote on May 21, 2025 (vote 276, agreed 51-46); the passage vote 277 on May 22, 2025 is the one recorded. On vote 277, Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) voted Yea; Blackburn, Budd, Tillis, Heinrich and Merkley did not vote.
H.J.Res. 35 (methane Waste Emissions Charge) Senate passage was Feb. 27, 2025 (vote 97); Kevin Cramer did not vote.
'Not in office' means the person was not a senator on the date of the vote (e.g., senators first seated in 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023 or 2025).

All votes taken from the Clerk of the House roll-call XML records: https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2022/roll420.xml, https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2025/roll190.xml, https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2025/roll052.xml, https://clerk.house.gov/evs/2025/roll114.xml. The Clerk records the 2025 H.R. 1 vote as Aye/No; these are normalized here to Yea/Nay.

Roster: Clerk MemberData.xml (https://clerk.house.gov/xml/lists/MemberData.xml, published 2026-10-01), cross-checked against the Clerk's member page counts (218 R, 214 D, 1 I, 2 vacancies). 433 voting representatives recorded; non-voting delegates and the Resident Commissioner are excluded. Vacant seats excluded: FL-20 (Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick resigned 2026-04-21) and TX-23 (Tony Gonzales resigned 2026-04-14). Any membership change after the Clerk data was published is not reflected.

Dates verified against the official record: H.J.Res. 35 (methane charge) passed the House on 2025-02-26 (roll 52); H.J.Res. 88 (California waiver) passed on 2025-05-01 (roll 114); H.R. 1 final passage was 2025-07-03 (roll 190); H.R. 5376 was 2022-08-12 (roll 420). The task descriptions were accurate.

Speaker Mike Johnson (LA-4) does not appear in the Clerk's roll 114 (H.J.Res. 88) record and is not counted in its party totals; he is shown as 'Not Voting' (by custom the Speaker votes only at his discretion). He is recorded as voting Yea/Aye on rolls 52 and 190 and Nay on roll 420.
Kevin Kiley (CA-3) is listed by the Clerk with party 'I' (caucusing with Republicans); he was a Republican at the time of the 2025 votes and was not in the House in August 2022.

Members not in office for any of the four votes (special-election or later arrivals): Adelita Grijalva (AZ-7), James Gallagher (CA-1), Aisha Wahab (CA-14), Everton Blair Jr. (GA-13), Clay Fuller (GA-14), Analilia Mejia (NJ-11), Matt Van Epps (TN-7), Christian Menefee (TX-18), James Walkinshaw (VA-11). Randy Fine (FL-6) and Jimmy Patronis (FL-1) took office 2025-04-02, after the methane vote.

On the 2022 IRA vote, all 220 Democrats voted Yea and 207 Republicans voted Nay; 4 Republicans did not vote (only Mike Rogers, AL-3, is still serving). On H.R. 1 (2025), Republicans Thomas Massie and Brian Fitzpatrick joined all Democrats voting No.
District numbers are as listed in current Clerk data; members first elected before 2022-2023 redistricting may have represented a different-numbered district at the time of the 2022 vote.
